claims.text: Module 1 is a 12-minute concepts lesson worth 100 EXP, has no prerequisites, covers Dash Core and Platform, quorums, ChainLocks, and InstantSend, and ends with quiz challenge what-is-dash-platform.
Dash Platform is a decentralized data-storage and application layer where developers define schemas and submit signed, structured state transitions rather than arbitrary user-written on-chain code.
Drive stores and validates Platform data, Platform supports indexed querying, and DAPI exposes decentralized access to Platform data and the Dash blockchain.
The Platform chain supplies layer 2 consensus and can read Core, while Core is not dependent on or aware of the Platform chain.
LLMQs are deterministic masternode subsets formed through distributed key generation and retained so they can produce BLS threshold signatures on consensus messages.
ChainLocks, deterministic InstantSend, and Platform use feature-specific quorum types rather than one universal quorum.
Platform reaches block finality through pBFT-based Tenderdash consensus; acceptance by at least two-thirds plus one of the validator set makes a Platform block final without reorganization.
Tenderdash uses rotating validator sets drawn from Platform LLMQs and recovered BLS threshold signatures, with quorum commitments recorded on Core.
Platform combines rapid BFT finality with validator and quorum membership rooted in Core's Proof-of-Work-secured state.
InstantSend automatically attempts to lock qualifying Core transaction inputs, with quorums conducting locking sessions and broadcasting a verifiable transaction-lock message.

ChainLocks threshold-sign the first Core block observed at a height, causing nodes to reject competing blocks at that height and any descendants of those competing blocks, which prevents reorganizations below the locked block.
ChainLock creation waits until every transaction in the Core block has an InstantSend lock, establishing retroactive locks where needed.
For identity funding, Dash is locked in a Core asset-lock transaction and Platform accepts either an InstantSend proof or proof that the transaction appears in a ChainLocked block.
Platform data is designed to be verifiable, with proof mechanics covered by the later Proofs lesson.

InstantSend and ChainLocks protect Core transactions and blocks, while Tenderdash quorum consensus finalizes Platform blocks; LLMQs connect the systems without giving both chains the same finality rule.
